W1-1.note: Vesna lifts out the sweet reed, fits a plainer one, and says a beginner has to hear her own mistakes.

W2-1.note: Vane's plan, which was carried, was to cut a second entrance through the sand spit at Low Point.

W2-2.note: Kerr's point was that the district office had made the same undertaking to two other towns and honored it in neither.

W2-3.note: The passage says directly that the Army engineer's dollar-for-dollar letter moved Pell and Danforth.

W2-4.note: The cut was carried by the promise of federal matching money, and it was opened to only nine of the fifteen feet planned.

W3-1.note: She had still not answered the library when the slips left for the capital.

W3-2.note: The passage closes with indignation on her behalf at a theft nobody has yet called one, and it rules out the other feelings.

W3-3.note: The second paragraph states she was certain people speak most truly while haggling, and C, D and A are each contradicted.

W3-4.note: 'A measure of oil' is a fixed quantity.

W3-5.note: The paragraph explains her market-day questioning of sellers and why she rejected written records, children's letters and correspondents.

W3-6.note: The passage centres on the capital compiler who printed eleven thousand of her entries under his name and never credited her.

W4-1.note: The second paragraph shows the mortgage closing off every other proposed use: pay in September or the yard shuts.

W4-2.note: Teodor sold the Marisol to the marina and signed the cheque over to the bank so the yard would stay open.

W4-3.note: 'The sale drew half the lake to the shed' means it attracted people in numbers.

W4-4.note: She was angry with him all evening and knew the anger was unfair.

W4-5.note: The marina sent a cheque, and on Friday he signed it over to the bank.

W4-6.note: Every option ended at the debt, and he says the yard outlasts any boat in it.

W5-1.note: The reviewer says that if the old tempo were restored the evening would collapse; the other four options describe conditions already true of this production.

W5-2.note: A score 'recopied from the 1961 parts' with errors corrected is written music.

W5-3.note: The review argues that the slower tempo alone does the work.

W5-4.note: 'It is the tempo', and the passage notes the other four changes did not actually happen.

W5-5.note: He says he has nothing to qualify, and he rules out relief (no rescue was needed), worry and fashion.

W6-1.note: 'The evidence is for salt', and the failures crowd the salty band below the culvert.

W6-2.note: He calls the work good but would take care carrying it beyond this ridge, and says he will not praise it without hedging.

W6-3.note: 'Flush the salt out and the shoots return.'

W6-4.note: 'A cold spring runs below the boundary rock' means water flowing steadily.

W6-5.note: The crew's evidence identifies road salt, and each alternative is ruled out.

W7-1.note: 'The club's conduct puzzles me', and praise, anger, hope and indifference are each denied explicitly.

W7-2.note: The surveys point to the dam trapping the silt the nymphs burrow in.

W7-3.note: The catch book dates the last big hatch to June 2010, and the passage denies that it does any of the other things.

W7-4.note: 'A spring feeds the north bay, a source of cold water.'

W7-5.note: 'Return depends on passing silt below the dam', and each other remedy is called useless.

W7-6.note: 'The surveys point to the dam', which has trapped the silt since 2009.
